output.summary: The yield decline is real: customer PPM rose, and CMM gauge R&R and inspection settings were unchanged. The new-operator cohort is ruled out, since their reject rates match experienced operators and yield fell before they ran alone. Three causes remain confounded: Corvane hardness spread, spindle wear after two deferred services, and 12-hour fatigue. Each coincides with the same weeks, and no discriminating comparison exists. Scrap-tag times are batch-written, so they say nothing about hour of machining. The deferral was caused by backlog pressure. Best next step is the staggered spindle service with Tamsworth trials and logging, plus the Line 6 CMM data and cycle-counter matching. Reject the sampling cut, the punishment of operators, and blaming any single cause to Halvard.
